subject: Custody models & fallback routing — next actions
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Stanton <emily.stanton@careport.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-12T15:05:00Z
Subject: Custody models & fallback routing — post-call recap

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps from Redwood's side.

Summary of what I heard
- Preferred deployment: leaning toward Dedicated capacity (single-tenant GPU pools) because you want predictable throughput and stronger isolation guarantees.
- Control plane: you asked about a Private control plane (VPC-hosted / customer-managed control plane) to meet audit boundaries, and BYOK/HSM integration for key custody.
- Data flow expectations: no cross-tenant co-mingling of model inputs/outputs, ability to restrict egress to CarePort-owned subnets, and a documented data deletion procedure for decommissioned model versions.
- Fallback behavior: you want an explicit fallback policy if Dedicated capacity is exhausted (e.g., auto-failover to an isolated Dedicated reserve or a Private VPC replica rather than the hosted multitenant API).

What we will provide next (owners & ETA)
- SOC2 scope summary + controls mapping (Marissa) — draft by EOD 12/13.
- Network diagram with recommended VPC peering/NAT/IAM boundaries and egress rules (Connor) — draft by 12/14.
- Sample SOW that outlines Dedicated capacity sizing, SLA, and fallback routing language (Jonas) — initial draft by 12/14.
- Tech deep-dive to validate KV caching, KV cache residency, and HSM integration — propose next-week slot (please share availability).

Open questions for your security/legal teams
1) BYOK requirement: Is an HSM-backed KMS mandatory for all encryption-at-rest, or only for key-rotation/backup keys?
2) Fallback policy: would CarePort accept a Dedicated reserve in the same account/tenant owned by Redwood but logically isolated, or must fallback be to a Private VPC instance under your control?
3) Egress whitelist: do you require a documented allowlist of IPs/subnets, or will CIDR ranges suffice?

Attachments referenced: SOC2 one-pager (we will send), sample network sketch (Connor to produce).

Next step: Emily, can you confirm who from your Security and Legal teams should receive the SOC2 summary and sample SOW? Also share 2–3 windows for a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

---
Note: attachment placeholders will follow in subsequent emails.

From: Emily Stanton <emily.stanton@careport.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: CarePort Security Team <security@careport.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Custody models & fallback routing — post-call recap

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from Security and Legal so you can tailor the deliverables.

Clarifications
- BYOK/HSM: Legal has stated they want HSM-backed keys for all customer data-at-rest related to model inputs/outputs. We need documentation on how Redwood handles key rotation, export controls, and access audits.
- Fallback policy: Preference is for failover to an instance we can control (Private VPC under CarePort). We are open to discussing a Redwood-managed Dedicated reserve only if we have contractual guarantees and cryptographic separation (separate key families).
- Egress: We require a CIDR-based allowlist plus an authenticated hostname pattern (for service endpoints).
- Data deletion: please include retention and proof-of-deletion options (e.g., API to trigger wipe + audit log entry).

People to include: please send the SOC2 summary and SOW to me and to two others on my side: Mark Alvarez (Infrastructure Lead, mark.alvarez@careport.com) and Priya Natarajan (Legal, priya.natarajan@careport.com). Security team copied here will review the network diagram.

Availability for deep-dive (EST):
- Tuesday 12/16: 11:00–12:30 or 15:00–16:00
- Wednesday 12/17: 09:00–10:00

We won't be moving to an on-prem option right now; the decision is between Dedicated with Private control plane (preferred) or Redwood-managed Dedicated with cryptographic separation.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Stanton
Head of Product Security | CarePort
emily.stanton@careport.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Custody models & fallback routing — next actions (internal owners)

Marissa/Connor — forwarding Emily's clarifications. Action items summarized below so we can move quickly. Emily is copying Mark and Priya on the next exchange.

Action items (owners)
- Marissa: finalize SOC2 scope one-pager and a controls mapping that specifically calls out encryption-at-rest, key custody, key rotation, and export controls. Deliverable: soc2_summary.pdf (draft) by 12/13 EOD.
- Connor: produce a network diagram that shows two alternatives: (A) Private control plane under CarePort VPC with peering and egress allowlist, (B) Redwood-managed Dedicated reserve with explicit cryptographic separation (distinct KMS key family). Deliverable: network_diagram_v1.png by 12/14.
- Jonas: assemble an initial SOW that includes Dedicated capacity sizing, SLA targets, fallback routing language, and legal-friendly language for key custody and deletion proofs. Deliverable: redwood_sample_sow_draft.docx by 12/14. 

Notes for the SOW/fallback language: avoid ambiguous wording like "best effort" for fallback. If we propose Redwood-managed reserve as fallback, include specific measurable terms (max failover time, isolation guarantees, key separation details, and audit rights).

Emily — we'll drop drafts into the link I've shared and follow up with a deep-dive invite for one of your proposed windows.

Jonas
